title: The workload as music director in California
summary: Welburn notes his health; McRae recalls the phone calls, broadcast changes and band problems on the Armstrong coast stay.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well you seemed to have been blessed with good health through all of this --
-- straw boss and the responsibility and taken it well.
Well this is the thing that kept you from --

See, if you were really interested in what you were doing and people put this on you -- I remember that time when we went to California when I had the Louie Armstrong, we were doing like two broadcast from coast to coast, and two local broadcasts that came as far as Chicago. Now the guy say, "Oh, you got more air time than God," you know. The song pluggers used to run me to death. On the switchboard, they had to put another girl on because Duke was in town, Jimmy was in town, Basie was in town, and all the telephone was coming in to Louie Armstrong.

Because Louie is on doing these pictures, he's doing --the command performance is coming up -- all these different things that was coming up, Joe Glaser was calling him on the coast to get this in and get (inaudible).
They put another girl on the whole time we were there for a month, you know. Just answering out telephone calls.
CBS was calling us and knocking us off the songs -- you can't do this song, you can't do that song.
Give me another song for this spot, give me another song for that spot. All that's going on all the time.
You got to be (inaudible) for that. So I just sat up in the room and write and stay there and get my telephone calls (inaudible) worry about what's going on, you know.
And then taking care of the band that run you half nuts half the time, you know. And things like that.
When you're on the road travelling, you
